title: End-of-unit quiz: forces, magnets and light
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Forces, magnets and light (Mighty Metals and Why Do Cat's Eyes Glow at Night?)
source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 18 (End-of-unit quiz: forces, magnets and light (portal quiz))
intro: Covers lessons 9 to 18 of Forces, magnets and light (Mighty Metals and Why Do Cat's Eyes Glow at Night?). Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: A toy car rolls on four surfaces. Where will it go furthest?
questions.a: C) Smooth wooden floor. The smooth floor has the least friction, so the car travels furthest.
B) A steel paper clip. Steel contains iron, so the paper clip is pulled by the magnet.

questions.q: Which can will a magnet pick up?
questions.a: B) A steel food tin. Steel contains iron, so it is magnetic. Aluminium and copper are metals but not magnetic.

questions.q: Two north poles are brought together. What happens?
questions.a: B) They repel. Like poles repel.
C) A torch. A torch gives out its own light. The others reflect light.
B) Aluminium foil. Foil is smooth and shiny, so it reflects the most light.
C) A wooden block. Wood is opaque: it blocks all the light.
B) Midday. The Sun is highest at midday, so shadows are shortest.
